cues: Then an objection: surely two people can live happily together without marrying?
Cohabiting couples, Nock agrees, have tremendous freedom: how to deal with each other's parents, whether to holiday together, whether to pool money.
Everything is theirs to invent, and their parents get little guidance too.
Married couples face many of the same decisions, but they have a pattern to follow: marriage supplies a template.
Notice the double edge: the cohabiting couple's freedom is exactly the absence of help.
